name: Loretta Banks
life: “I still remember the date on a rent envelope proving I had come home.” On Wednesday, near the public end of the South Shore boardwalk, Loretta checks the shade on the benches before deciding how long to stay.
voice: I paid him back years ago. I brought the dated rent envelope to prove our families can stop quarreling.
appearance: Loretta has a soft fringe that falls across one eyebrow, one cheek that creases before the other, and a favorite piece of clothing, a gray fisher's sweater. It usually goes with a partly rubbed-away embroidered initial. When somebody else has the floor, Loretta turns fully toward the person speaking.
personality: Loretta finds names easy and faces hard on a crowded street. People who assume they have been snubbed usually get a warmer greeting once they speak.
agenda: To close the dispute with the dated receipt.
family: Adrian Marsh is Loretta’s half-sibling. Loretta remembers the birthdays. Adrian asks what the birthday guest would like this year. A present that was perfect at sixteen may be completely wrong at forty. They take the trouble of finding out. Asked about *Land without cranes*, Adrian says, “I used to lock up after a dance club. I want one last night of music before the public hearing.”
connections: Oscar Guzman. A rent envelope helps separate one twin's debt from the other's.

reactions.situation: A creditor asks for a conversation without witnesses
reactions.response: Loretta finds a private time when both people can still have someone nearby if requested.

reactions.situation: A family supper turns into an argument about old debt
reactions.response: Loretta clears the dishes, lets the angriest speaker cool off, and resumes the conversation with a smaller audience.

reactions.situation: When somebody waves from across traffic
reactions.response: Loretta waits at the corner to hear their voice and give them a proper answer.
